questions.q: Given $\cos\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}$ and $\theta$ in the fourth quadrant, find $\sin\theta$ and $\tan\theta$.
questions.answer: $\sin^2\theta=1-\dfrac{16}{25}=\dfrac{9}{25}$. In the fourth quadrant, sine is negative: $\sin\theta=-\dfrac{3}{5}$. $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{-3/5}{4/5}=-\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.q: Use the sum identity to find the exact value of $\sin(75^\circ)$, using $\sin(75^\circ)=\sin(45^\circ+30^\circ)$.
questions.answer: $\sin(45^\circ+30^\circ)=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}$.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ in the first quadrant, find $\sin(2\theta)$ and $\cos(2\theta)$.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}$ (first quadrant, positive). $\sin(2\theta)=2\sin\theta\cos\theta=2\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)=\dfrac{24}{25}$. $\cos(2\theta)=1-2\sin^2\theta=1-2\left(\dfrac{9}{25}\right)=1-\dfrac{18}{25}=\dfrac{7}{25}$.

questions.q: State the amplitude, period, and phase shift of $y=2\sin\left(3x-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
questions.answer: Amplitude: $2$. Period: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$. Phase shift: solve $3x-\dfrac{\pi}{2}=0$, giving $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ (shift right by $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$).

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arcsin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.
questions.answer: $\arcsin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ (or $30^\circ$), since $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ is in the range of arcsine.

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arccos\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$.
questions.answer: $\arccos\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ (or $135^\circ$), since $\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is in the range of arccosine.

questions.q: Solve $2\cos^2\theta-1=0$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. Solutions: $\theta=45^\circ,135^\circ,225^\circ,315^\circ$.

questions.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time, one traveling at $20^\circ$ and the other at $80^\circ$ (measured from north), each at 15 mph. Find the distance between the ships after 2 hours, to the nearest mile, using the Law of Cosines.
questions.answer: Each ship travels $15(2)=30$ miles. The angle between their paths: $80^\circ-20^\circ=60^\circ$. Using the Law of Cosines: $d^2=30^2+30^2-2(30)(30)\cos60^\circ=900+900-1800(0.5)=1800-900=900$. $d=\sqrt{900}=30$ miles.

questions.q: Convert the polar point $\left(4,\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ to rectangular coordinates.
questions.answer: $x=r\cos\theta=4\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=2$. $y=r\sin\theta=4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=4\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=2\sqrt{3}$. Rectangular coordinates: $(2,2\sqrt{3})$.

sections.heading: A multi-part trigonometric identity verification problem

questions.q: This question has two parts. (a) Use the identity $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ together with the double angle formulas to derive a formula for $\tan(2\theta)$ in terms of $\tan\theta$. (b) Use your formula to find $\tan(2\theta)$ given $\tan\theta=3$.
questions.answer: (a) $\tan(2\theta)=\dfrac{\sin(2\theta)}{\cos(2\theta)}=\dfrac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta}$. Dividing numerator and denominator by $\cos^2\theta$: $\tan(2\theta)=\dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1-\tan^2\theta}$. (b) $\tan(2\theta)=\dfrac{2(3)}{1-9}=\dfrac{6}{-8}=-\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.q: Use the half-angle identity to find $\cos(15^\circ)$, given $\cos(30^\circ)=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
questions.answer: Half-angle identity: $\cos\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\cos\theta}{2}}$. With $\theta=30^\circ$: $\cos(15^\circ)=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2+\sqrt{3}}{4}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3}}}{2}$.

questions.q: Solve $2\sin^2\theta-\sin\theta-1=0$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$.
questions.answer: This factors as a quadratic in $\sin\theta$: $(2\sin\theta+1)(\sin\theta-1)=0$, so $\sin\theta=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ or $\sin\theta=1$. For $\sin\theta=1$: $\theta=90^\circ$. For $\sin\theta=-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $\theta=210^\circ$ or $\theta=330^\circ$. All solutions: $90^\circ,210^\circ,330^\circ$.

questions.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 and 12, and included angle $50^\circ$, using $\text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
questions.answer: Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(12)\sin(50^\circ)\approx\dfrac{1}{2}(96)(0.766)\approx36.8$.

questions.q: Simplify $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta+\tan^2\theta$ in terms of $\sec\theta$.
questions.answer: Since $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, the expression becomes $1+\tan^2\theta$. Using the Pythagorean identity $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$, the simplified expression is $\sec^2\theta$.

sections.heading: A multi-part navigation and triangulation problem

questions.q: This question has three parts. A hiker walks 5 miles due east, then turns and walks 7 miles at a bearing of $40^\circ$ north of east. (a) Find the angle between the two legs of the hike (measured as the interior angle at the turning point). (b) Use the Law of Cosines to find the straight-line distance from the start to the end point, to the nearest tenth of a mile. (c) Explain why this distance is less than the total distance walked (12 miles).
questions.answer: (a) The second leg deviates $40^\circ$ from due east, so the interior angle at the turn (between reversing the first leg's direction and the second leg) is $180^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$. (b) $d^2=5^2+7^2-2(5)(7)\cos(140^\circ)=25+49-70(-0.766)\approx74+53.6\approx127.6$. $d\approx\sqrt{127.6}\approx11.3$ miles. (c) The straight-line distance is always less than or equal to the sum of the individual leg lengths (a consequence of the triangle inequality) — walking in two different directions doesn't add distance as efficiently as walking directly toward the destination, since the path bends rather than going straight.

questions.q: Verify the identity $\dfrac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta}=\sin\theta$.
questions.answer: Using the Pythagorean identity, $1-\cos^2\theta=\sin^2\theta$. Substituting: $\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta}=\sin\theta$ (for $\sin\theta\neq0$), confirming the identity holds.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle measure 7 and 8, with an included angle of 120$^\circ$. Find the length of the third side, using the Law of Cosines.
questions.answer: Using the Law of Cosines with $\cos(120^\circ)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $c^2=7^2+8^2-2(7)(8)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=49+64+56=169$, so $c=\sqrt{169}=13$.
